This attack can be used every 2 seconds when within 1.2 meters of a player. === Throw === Winds their arm back before swinging forward to throw a rock (10 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] damage). The rock travels at 12 meters per second for up to 4 seconds before despawning and has a spread of 5 degrees. This attack can be used every 8 seconds when within 5–15 meters of a player. == Gallery == File:Valheim Greydwarf-1 ver0-79-10.jpg File:One-star greydwarf.png|A One-Star Greydwarf. Note the red bark. File:Two-star greydwarf.png|A Two-Star Greydwarf. Note the blue bark and accents. File:2Star Greydwarf.png|2 star Greydwarf == Notes == * The word Greydwarf is derived from Astrid Lindgren's tale Ronja the Robber's daughter (Ronja Rövardotter). Originally named Grådvärgar, which is literally translated to Greydwarves. They are short creatures with grey fur who will attack a person when they sense the victim's fear. If you are emotionally aggressive then they will leave you be. == Lore == {{Quote|Let all who read me beware of the Greydwarfs, the skulkers in darkness, the soulless ones. They are born from rot and rainfall, they spring like mushrooms from the smoking soil. There is nothing on their tongues or behind their eyes, those who fear nothing should still fear them. When the soul of a murderer or a great sinner rots under the ground, it makes a hollow cyst which draws rock and wood and moss to it. It gathers up the peat into flesh, braids reeds into bone and takes rags for skin. It should not walk but when the night comes it walks. Should you who read this see one with a sword to your hand, lance it and let it out. Or put it to the torch, for it fears the flame.|[[Runestone]]}} The runestones' portrayal of the Greydwarfs is racially motivated: they stereotype the entire race as "the skulkers in darkness, the soulless ones", with "nothing on their tongues or behind their eyes",In-game text, Greydwarf runestone ($lore_greydwarfs). and one urges travelers not to pity them: "Raised by the Old Man of the Forest from seeds of sin, the greydwarfs clothe themselves in the human forms they once knew, but there is no longer any warmth in their hearts. They live now only to serve the Elder and to protect the wood. Do not let pity for them stay your hand."In-game text, Black Forest runestone ($lore_blackforest_random09). == References == {{Creatures}} [[ru:Грейдворф]] [[fr:Naingris]] [[cs:Šedý trpaslík]] [[uk:Сіролюд]] [[de:Grauzwerg]] __NOTOC__

They are small flaming imps that are relatively weak, especially in [[Swamp]]s where the constant raining significantly reduces the damage from their ranged fireball attack. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Surtlings|Aggressive creature strategies#Surtling}} Surtlings spawning near [[Fire geysers]] can be farmed through lowering the ground around the spawn area with a pickaxe. As soon as the Surtling spawns in water, it will take damage and quickly die. === Fireball === Winds back before tossing a ball of fire at the player, which applies the [[Burning]] status (10 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] and 40 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]] damage). This attack has a 3-second cooldown and can be used within 10 meters of a player. The fireball travels at 11 meters per second for up to 4 seconds before despawning and has a spread of 2–20 degrees. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Coal|0star=4|1star=8|2star=16}} {{drop row|item=Surtling core| 0star=50%|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Surtling trophy|0star=5%| 1star=5%|2star=5%}}}} == Spawning == {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=3 [[spawn points]] near [[Fire geysers]]|frequency=Respawn after 5 minutes}} {{spawn row|type=During "There's a smell of sulfur in the air..."  == Lore == {{Quote|Let you who read me know of the Surtlings, that you might not fall prey to their wickedness. Long ago the great demon Surtr was brought down and destroyed by the First Men, giant warriors of whom you are but a dwindling echo. They smote long upon the body of this Surtr with swords and hammers so that his fiery substance was shattered into many small pieces. He who was made of the fire was fire in every part of him. You could not say ‘Here is the brain of Surtr’ or ‘Here is Surtr’s liver’ because every part was Surtr. So all the fragments of him were Surtr still, only much weaker in power and in thought and in memory, with no way to become whole once again. Now we call these fragments Surtlings and when they are found they should be stamped out like the last embers of a fire or doused with water to choke off their flames at the root. They will throw fire from afar and joy in causing terror and destruction. Even in his scattered dotage, the demon seeks revenge on the children of the First Men.|[[Runestone]]}} {{Creatures}} [[ru:Суртлинг]] [[uk:Вогневик]] [[fr:Surtling]] [[cs:Surtling]] [[de:Surtling]]

He appears as a towering humanoid tree-like entity with multiple thin branches sprouting out of his slender, bark-covered body. == Summoning == [[File:TheElderAltar.png|left|thumb|200x200px|The Elder's Forsaken Altar.]] The Elder's [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] is located in [[Black Forest|Black Forests]]. His location can be revealed when visiting [[Burial Chambers]] and sometimes ruined structures around Black Forests, where a [[Runestone|Vegvisir]] will reveal his nearest summoning location on the map. He is summoned by placing three {{Item Link|Ancient Seed}}s in his Forsaken altar in Black Forests. Like all bosses, the Elder can be summoned as many times as desired, provided the required materials are met. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating the Elder|Boss strategies#The Elder}} The Elder has an environment aura that removes darkness and raining. === Root Spawn === The Elder will raise an arm in the air to summon 15 hostile [[Root (creature)|Roots]] within a 15-meter radius circle around the player. Roots can attack players in melee range but are otherwise immobile and will despawn after 18–20 seconds or when The Elder is defeated. Although not typically possible in regular gameplay, a maximum of 30 Roots can be active at once. This ability has a 25-second cooldown and can be used while within 30 meters of a player. === Shoot === A ranged volley of 25 vines directed at a target player (35 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 20 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 20 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage per hit). This attack has a 6-second cooldown and can be used when a player is 15–50 meters away. He attempts to track players while aiming. Each vine has an initial velocity of 30 meters per second and a spread of 10–20 degrees. They can travel for up to 6 seconds before disappearing. === Stomp === A close-range stomp over a large area (60 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). It hits in a circle 5 meters in radius from the impact point. This attack can be used when within 3 meters of a player and is accessible every 5 seconds. == Aftermath == Defeating the Elder allows the player to unlock and enter swamp crypts (which are the primary source of [[Scrap Iron]] in the game) with the [[Swamp Key]]. === Drops === {{drop table|{{drop row|item=The Elder trophy|0star=1}} {{drop row|item=Swamp key|0star=1 per player}} |stars=0}} === Forsaken power === Mounting The Elder’s trophy upon his respective stone will allow the player to claim his Forsaken Power. This ability will grant the player and nearby allies the following effects for 300 seconds: * Health regen: +30% * Chop damage: +60% * Pickaxe damage: +60% === Events === Defeating The Elder affects the following [[events]] for that world: * Disables: "The forest is moving..." * Enables: "A foul smell from the swamp..." (if [[Bonemass]] has not been defeated) * Enables: "The ground is shaking." (if a [[Troll]] has died in the world) === Creature spawning === Defeating The Elder unlocks several creatures to spawn at '''night''' in unusual biomes. They can only have 0 stars: * [[Greydwarf Brute]] in Meadows. * [[Greydwarf Shaman]] in Meadows. * [[Draugr]] while it is "Misty" in Meadows, Black Forest, Mountain, Plains. * [[Odin]] in Meadows, Black Forest, Plains. === Traders === Defeating The Elder unlocks the [[Thunder Stone]] and [[Ymir Flesh]] for sale from [[Haldor]]. It also unlocks the [[Woodland Herb Blend]] from [[The Bog Witch]] for 120 [[Coins]]. == Gallery == File:Elder and friends.jpg File:TheElderAltar.png == Notes == * The altar provides a few hints on what items are used to summon him. First, the altar reads "Burn their young" referring to [[Ancient Seed]]s. In addition, the top of the columns are topped by statues that look similar to Ancient Seeds in shape. * Because of The Elder's location in the [[Black Forest]], additional enemies such as [[Troll]]s or [[Greydwarf]]s may join the battle and increase the difficulty significantly, especially at night. * The Elder's high-damage ranged attack can be effective in quickly gathering resources such as [[Wood]], [[Corewood]], [[Stone]], and [[Copper Ore]], without the use of tools. * In the in-game trophies menu, there is another description of The Elder, "Even in death, it seems to grin with secret knowledge." * When The Elder's trophy is mounted on an item mount, he will sometimes say: "Little thing of blood and bone, I should have snapped you like a twig! Now I wither and die, let the great tree have me..." The many names of The Elder: * In the game files, The Elder is also known as "gd_king" as well as "theelder". Likely to be interpreted as "Greydwarf King". * Warnings inscribed in a few of the [[Runestone|runestones]] found in the [[Black Forest]] refer to The Elder as "the One Who Walks" once, and "the Old One" twice:
''Beneath the ground, the roots of the forest twine together on a great loom. Pluck one thread and the whole weave will move. Chop down one tree and all the wood will know. Make yourself known to the One Who Walks, and he will seek you out.''
''Beware the Old One. The ravens say that in ages past he was a shoot of great Yggdrasil itself and a force of wisdom in the days when men and trees were friends. Now he scorns the axe and sets himself against the works of the Gods themselves. Odin banished him here for his pride but his roots are deep.''
''Seven were the creatures banished to this world by mighty Odin in the first days of his kingship. Seven gods and monsters too proud to bear his yoke. I have heard the tread of the Old Ones in the forest and have crouched in the shadow of the Mountain Mother when she flies. Of the others I know little. I will add to this stone when I have seen more.''

[[Beech Seeds]]}} Beech is a type of tree that can be found in the [[Meadows]] biome. It is characterized by its light grey bark and wide crown. Beech can be found in small and large variants. {{image link|Wooden atgeir|size=48px}}{{image link|Wooden greatsword|size=48px}} |} == Properties== ===Wielding (One-handed/Two-handed)=== Only '''one-handed weapons''' can be simultaneously equipped with [[shields]] or a [[Torch]]. All melee '''two-handed weapons''' have a greater movement speed reduction and cannot be used together with shields or a torch. ===[[Damage and Blocking Mechanics|Offensive and defensive properties]]=== ====Damage/Damage type==== All damages in ''[[Valheim]]'' have a '''damage type'''. Some [[creatures]] have weaknesses/resistances to certain [[damage types]], which increases/decreases the effectiveness of these damages. For example, [[Skeleton]]s are weak to blunt damage and resist pierce damage. When creatures are hit by damage with damage types they are weak/resist to, the damage numbers would be shown in yellow/grey color compared to the usual white color. Similar types of weapons mostly deal the same type of damage: *Blunt damage: One/two-handed [[Clubs]] *Slash damage: One/two-handed [[Axes]], [[Swords]] *Pierce damage: [[Spears]], [[Polearms]], [[Pickaxes]], [[Bows]] *Half slash, half pierce damage: [[Knives]] Exceptions include weapons that deal elemental damage like [[Torch]], [[Frostner]] and [[Draugr fang]]. Some [[clubs]] including [[Stagbreaker]] and [[Porcupine]] also deal pierce damage besides blunt damage. Keep in mind that not all damage types are upgraded when upgrading some weapons. ====Block armor and block force==== All weapons have a value of block armor, indicating the amount of damage absorbed when blocked by the weapon. Block force shows the amount of knockback applied to enemies when blocked. ====[[Parry|Parry and Parry bonus]]==== Weapons and shields, except tower [[shields]], can be used to parry attacks, with varying parry bonuses. Parry bonus is a multiplier to block armor (damage absorbed) when parrying. Damage dealt to the enemy in a period of time after a successful parry that absorbs all the damage is always 2x. Parry bonus is mostly determined by the weapon type: *Tower [[shields]]: Cannot parry *[[Tankard]], [[Bows]], Round [[shields]]: 1.5x *Buckler [[shields]]: 2.5x *[[Polearms]] (atgeirs): 3x *[[Knives]]: 4x *[[Flesh rippers]]: 6x *All other weapons: 2x ====Backstab==== Backstab indicates the multiplier applied to enemies when backstabbing. The backstab bonus is applied when attacking unaware enemies, regardless of whether they are facing towards or away from the player. Backstabbing an enemy gives it a backstab immunity for 5 minutes. Backstabbing can occur even if the enemy has partial HP. An enemy which has a red exclamation point over its name and HP bar, indicating that it is aware of your location, cannot be backstabbed. *[[Abyssal Harpoon]]: 1x *Two-handed [[clubs]]: 2x *[[Tankard]] (Cannot attack): 4x *[[Knives]] and [[Flesh rippers]]: 6x *All other weapons, including [[bows]] and one-handed [[clubs]]: 3x ====Knockback==== Knockback shows how far enemies are knocked back when attacked by the weapon. ===Movement speed=== Most weapons, when equipped, decrease the character's movement speed and increase dodge roll cost. The movement speed effect is mostly determined by the weapon type: *[[Flesh Rippers]] and [[Knives]]: -0% (No movement speed reduction) *All other one-handed melee weapons, [[Bows]], non-Tower [[Shields]], [[Pickaxes]], [[Polearms]], and [[Magic]]: -5% *[[Serpent Scale Shield]]: -15% *Two-handed [[Axes]], two-handed [[Clubs]], and [[Shields|Tower Shields]] other than [[Serpent Scale Shield]]: -20% == Melee weapons == Melee weapons are [[items]] that can be equipped to increase attack damage. Different types of melee weapon can have different ranges, attack speeds, stamina costs per attack and secondary attacks. When equipping one-handed weapons, the character can also equip [[shields]]. Most melee weapons' attack pattern involve a 3-hit combo. Generally, the first hit has the slowest delay (from the initial click), the second hit has less delay, and the third hit is slightly slower while dealing the most damage. Most melee weapons are quicker to recover and block from a miss than after a direct strike. Below are details regarding each type of melee weapon: === [[Axes]] === Axes are the only type of weapon that can be used to cut down trees. The '''Eitr Refinery''' is a structure used for processing {{Item Link|Sap}} and {{Item Link|Soft Tissue}} into {{Item Link|Refined Eitr}}.

== Building ==
Eitr Refinery is unlocked once the player has the required materials. A [[Black Metal Axe]] is required to obtain [[Yggdrasil Wood]], and a [[Sap Extractor]] is required to obtain [[Sap]]. The sap extractor requires a [[Dvergr Extractor]] obtained from [[Dvergr Component Crate]]s in Dvergr settlements. [[Infested Mine]]s must also be explored to obtain [[Black Core]]s.

Eitr Refineries can be constructed on flat terrain or on stone floors, but degrade from rain when not under a roof.

== Usage ==
Up to 20 [[Sap]] can be supplied into the funnel at the front of the refinery, and up to 20 [[Soft Tissue]] can be inserted into the grinder at the top. It is possible to climb to the top of the grinder, but constructing stairs makes accessing it easier. The resulting [[Refined Eitr]] is ejected from the tube next to the sap input, opposite the grinder.

The sap:soft tissue ratio is roughly 20:20. Each sap (acting as a fuel) adds 40 seconds, and the operating time on a full fuel tank is 800 seconds. But filling both the Sap and Soft tissue slots to the max will consume 20 Soft tissue and 19 Sap to produce 20 Refined eitr, leaving 1 Sap (probably due to a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-off_error round-off error]).

While processing, small discharges are emitted from the structure, inflicting Lightning and Poison [[Damage]] over time. The eitr dropped on the ground will also emit these discharges, which will eventually damage and destroy structures not immune to elemental damage. Structures immune to elemental damage include [[Cage Wall 2x2|iron]] and [[Dvergr metal wall|copper]] cage pieces, and [[Black Marble]] floor/wall/pillars. Wood and ordinary stone structures will take damage. 

== Notes ==
* As with other [[Mistlands]]-tier structures and items, this can theoretically be obtained before building a [[Wisp Fountain]], but navigation is made difficult by the intense mist.

The '''Sap Extractor''' is a structure used to harvest {{Item link|Sap}} from [[Ancient Roots]] in the [[Mistlands]] [[Biomes|biome]].

==Building==
Sap Extractors can be built on Ancient Roots within the range of a [[Workbench]].

It requires [[Black Metal]], [[Yggdrasil Wood]] and a [[Dvergr Extractor]], obtained from [[Dvergr Component Crate]]s.

==Usage==
When placed on [[Ancient Roots]], the Sap Extractor will extract {{Item link|Sap|1}} from the root every 60 seconds. It can hold a maximum of 10 Sap and glows green if it contains any Sap to harvest. As it is extracting, green particles will leave the top and bottom of the extractor. The particles will stop appearing at the top once the extractor is full, or if attempting to extract from a completely dried root.

As Ancient Roots regenerate Sap much slower than it is extracted, at 1 sap per {{duration|400}} (see their page for details). It is strategic to relocate extractors between multiple roots. Destroying or deconstructing an extractor with Sap inside does not drop the Sap.

==Tips==
* The required Black Metal cannot easily be teleported to the extraction site:
** Therefore, it is advisable to transport some by [[Boat]] before setting off to explore the Mistlands. Ideally, scout the biome for a location with many Ancient Roots as well as tillable ground in proximity, and if so, carry over the Black Metal and set up an outpost.
** Alternatively, the Mistlands biome are generally close to the [[Plains]], so it is possible to acquire [[Black Metal Scrap]] on site. The [[Iron]] needed to build a [[Blast Furnace]] can be mined from [[Ancient Sword]] or [[Ancient Armor]]. All other materials can be teleported via [[Portal]].

'''Unstable Lava Rocks''' are resource nodes found in the [[Ashlands]] biome, being a source of {{Item link|Proustite Powder}}.

When destroyed by receiving 50 or more damage from any weapon or a [[pickaxe]], they explode. The explosion damages surrounding objects, including players, creatures and structures. Additionally, it creates a small crater in the ground.

== Availability ==
Unstable Lava Rocks can often be found attached to large boulders and stones in the [[Ashlands]] biome, as well as on the ground occasionally.
